newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures see short covering rally at close.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures see short covering rally at close.

text.p: IPE Brent closed firmer on Monday, after last minute short covering pulled the market up.
IPE Oct Brent settled up seven cents at $22.61 a barrel having flirted with $22.73 and toyed with $22.31 during the day.
Short covering in the last 15 minutes of trading saw prices rise from $22.45 a barrel in thinish volume.
"There was some local short covering. People would rather be flat than be caught with shorts overnight and the market ran up in thin volume," said one IPE trader.
The market tone was firm and steadier after last week's surges.
"It (Monday) was a breathing space as people weighed up the reasons for a further rise," commented one IPE trader.
Dealers said there was no fresh news from Iraqi that was impacting the market compared with last week.
The Oct/Nov spread widened slightly to +69 cents a barrel against Friday's +64 cents.

The loss of strength of October Brent was partly related to weakness in products, particuarly IPE gas oil which settled $2.50 down at $217.50. The Brent/gas oil crack was a touch softer at $5.64, a barrel. A weaker NYMEX was also bearish on Brent.
Dealers said gas oil was correcting after last week's rally with some clearing of positions before the September contract's expiry on Thursday.
Funds were seen rolling over their September positions into October. The Sept/October backwardation eased to $8.25 a tonne, $1 off Friday, but still firm.
Traders said gas oil may have lost ground, but the tone was still firm. "There was plenty to give back," commented one trader refering to last week's surge.
